key_insight: The paper finds that low-bit quantized models fail at long-form reasoning not just because of lower precision, but because training on fixed prefixes creates a mismatch with the model’s own generated tokens. Training on the quantized model’s actual rollout trajectories reduces repetitive loops and improves reasoning stability.
problem_solved: It addresses the severe drop in mathematical and code reasoning performance that remains after quantization-aware distillation, especially in sub-3-bit models where long answers often spiral into repetition and fail to finish.
method: Identify quantization-amplified exposure bias as the core cause of long-generation failures.
Train distillation on-policy, using trajectories generated by the quantized model rather than only fixed corpus prefixes.
Align supervision with the model’s own autoregressive behavior to make reasoning more robust under low-bit inference.
impact: For practitioners deploying compact models, this offers a practical path to better reasoning quality without increasing bit-width. It is especially relevant for edge deployment and cost-sensitive systems where decoding stability matters as much as raw accuracy.

paper_title: Train Where the Quantized Model Goes: On-Policy Distillation for Low-Bit Reasoning
paper_authors: Yuanteng Chen, Zhilei Liu, Peisong Wang, Yuantian Shao, Chuangyi Li
